sections.section_title: Case Presentation and Initial Clinical Clues
sections.description: Introduces the patient’s presentation and the early findings that prompted consideration of monogenic diabetes rather than classic type 1 or type 2 diabetes.
subtopics: Demographics and vitals: young adult male; BMI 24.6 kg/m2; BP 112/70 mmHg; HR 78 bpm
Symptoms and screening context: glycosuria on annual exam; hyperglycaemia; polydipsia, polyphagia; recent weight loss; no diabetic ketoacidosis
Physical exam: no acanthosis nigricans or other overt insulin-resistance stigmata
Baseline glycaemia: HbA1c 10.2% (88 mmol/mol); fasting glucose 12.4 mmol/L; 2-hour OGTT 19.8 mmol/L
Lipid profile: HDL 1.01 mmol/L; triglycerides 4.31 mmol/L—possible metabolic syndrome despite limited clinical insulin-resistance signs
Family history pattern suggesting autosomal dominant early-onset diabetes: maternal grandmother (30s), mother (late 20s), brother (age 20)
Early complication screen: no microalbuminuria; markedly reduced hand sudomotor function indicating small-fibre autonomic dysfunction

sections.description: Explains how HNF1A mutations cause the phenotype observed, and situates the patient’s novel variant within functional domains and inheritance patterns.
subtopics: HNF1A basics: gene at 12q24; 10 exons; protein expressed in pancreas, liver, kidneys; domains (dimerization, DNA-binding, transactivation)
Beta-cell dysfunction mechanisms: reduced insulin and GLUT2 gene expression; diminished pyruvate kinase activity; progressive fall in insulin secretion and postprandial hyperglycaemia
Renal tubular effects: reduced SGLT2 expression under HNF1A control lowers renal glucose threshold, producing glycosuria
Typical HNF1A-MODY phenotype: adolescent/young-adult onset; non-autoimmune; strong autosomal dominant transmission; early sulfonylurea sensitivity; minimal insulin resistance initially
Patient’s variant: heterozygous c.809A>G (p.N270S) in exon 4 within the DNA-binding domain; absent from ClinVar/VarSome—novel finding

Evidence for pathogenicity (ACMG-aligned): segregation with diabetes in family; high in silico deleteriousness (AlphaMissense 0.995); location in critical domain; rarity—supporting likely pathogenic classification

Brief contrast with other MODY types relevant to management: GCK-MODY (mild stable hyperglycaemia; usually no treatment), HNF4A-MODY (macrosomia/neonatal hypoglycaemia), HNF1B-MODY (renal/urogenital anomalies)

sections.section_title: Diagnostic Reasoning: From Differential to Genetic Confirmation
sections.description: Details the stepwise evaluation distinguishing MODY from type 1 and type 2 diabetes and the decisive role of genetic testing.
subtopics: Initial differential in young-onset diabetes: type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, MODY, secondary causes
Clinical discriminators favouring MODY: young age; non-ketotic presentation; multigenerational early-onset diabetes; glycosuria disproportionate to plasma glucose; absence of acanthosis
Autoimmunity assessment: negative GAD and IA-2 antibodies; note that occasional antibody positivity can occur in MODY

Beta-cell reserve: glucagon-stimulated C-peptide 0.83 nmol/L (>0.60 nmol/L suggests preserved endogenous insulin); fasting C-peptide 0.39 nmol/L—supports non–type 1 diabetes yet indicates beta-cell dysfunction
Glycaemic pattern: marked postprandial hyperglycaemia on OGTT (2-hour 19.8 mmol/L) consistent with HNF1A-MODY physiology
Predictive tools: Exeter MODY probability calculator (62.4% in this case) and limitations in non-European populations
Genetic confirmation strategy: indications to order an NGS MODY panel; interpreting variants under ACMG criteria to establish HNF1A-MODY
Baseline complication screening: urine albumin, retinal exam, and sudomotor testing—useful for staging and counselling but not diagnostic of MODY

sections.section_title: Precision Therapy in HNF1A-MODY: Rationale and Regimen
sections.description: Outlines treatment choices at presentation and after genetic confirmation, aligning pharmacology with HNF1A-MODY pathophysiology and evidence.
subtopics: Acute goals: reverse glucotoxicity and promptly control hyperglycaemia
Initial empiric regimen (pre-genetic result): basal insulin degludec 8 units/day + metformin 1500 mg/day + saxagliptin 5 mg/day—appropriate while T2D remains possible
Post-diagnostic tailoring: discontinue insulin; start dulaglutide 1.5 mg weekly; continue metformin—leveraging efficacy with low hypoglycaemia risk and potential beta-cell benefit
Evidence context: sulfonylureas are classic first-line in HNF1A-MODY; GLP-1 receptor agonists achieve similar control with fewer hypoglycaemic events and weight advantages
Maintenance strategy: transition to metformin + DPP-4 inhibitor once stable; plan for escalation as beta-cell function declines over time
Agents to avoid/caution: SGLT2 inhibitors—baseline SGLT2 downregulation increases risks of dehydration, genital infections, and (eu)DKA
Lifestyle therapy: structured nutrition, regular physical activity, education on hypoglycaemia and sick-day rules
Monitoring: individualized HbA1c target (often <6.5%); annual microalbuminuria and retinal screening; neuropathy follow-up; cardiovascular risk management
Family implications: cascade genetic testing and counselling for at-risk relatives

sections.description: Summarizes the patient’s course and distills actionable lessons to improve recognition and management of HNF1A-MODY.
subtopics: Glycaemic response: HbA1c improved from 10.2% to 9.1% at 1 month; to 6.0% by 6 months on GLP-1 RA; sustained <6.5% on metformin + saxagliptin
Complication status to date: no microalbuminuria or retinopathy; reduced sudomotor function warrants longitudinal follow-up
Prognosis: gradual beta-cell decline anticipated; adjust therapy over time while minimizing hypoglycaemia
Impact of precise diagnosis: de-intensified insulin use; aligned drug selection; improved safety and quality of life; informed family screening
When to suspect HNF1A-MODY: young-onset non-ketotic diabetes; strong autosomal dominant family history; glycosuria; negative islet antibodies; preserved C-peptide; minimal insulin-resistance signs
Pitfalls and safeguards: obesity/metabolic syndrome can coexist; calculators may misestimate in non-European groups; occasional antibody positivity; repeat C-peptide if uncertain
Research and registry value: novel p.N270S expands the HNF1A mutation spectrum—importance of database submission and ongoing genotype–phenotype correlation
